hook: This section of the FBI's 62-HQ-83894 file spans 1966–1977 and contains correspondence between J. Edgar Hoover's office and a NICAP member suspicious of the Amalgamated Flying Saucer Clubs of America (AFSCA), the AFSCA's 3rd National Convention program with its list of 'contactee' speakers, politically charged AFSCA newsletter content, and a 1977 White House inquiry—routed through Jody Powell of the Carter staff—asking the FBI about executive branch coordination on UFO information.
why_it_matters: The June 1977 White House memo reveals that a sitting president's press secretary (Jody Powell) formally raised the question of whether any executive branch coordination existed on UFO intelligence, indicating the issue reached the highest levels of government even after Project Blue Book's closure. The FBI's formal written response—that it lacks any 'conceivable jurisdiction' and routes all UFO information to the Air Force—documents the institutional vacuum that existed between agencies. The 1966 AFSCA materials show the FBI was actively filing civilian UFO organization publications, including contactee claims and politically subversive 'channeled messages,' as part of its internal records.

key_findings.finding: The Carter White House, through staffer Jody Powell, formally inquired whether any executive branch coordination existed on UFO information, reflecting high-level government interest in the post-Blue Book period.

quotes.text: He advised that Jody Powell of the President's staff has raised the question as to whether or not there is any coordination within the Executive Branch relating to information concerning this subject.

key_findings.finding: The FBI formally declared it had no jurisdiction over UFO sightings and was routing all such information to the Air Force without further action, documenting the agency's official stance of non-involvement.

quotes.text: I advised him that as far as the FBI is concerned there appears to be no conceivable jurisdiction for us to sengact any inquiries upon receipt of information relating to a UFO sighting and, in the absence of some investigative jurisdiction based upon the information furnished, that information would be referred to the Department of the Air Force without any action h\being taken by the Bureau.

In response to your inquiry, this Bureau is strictly an investigative agency of the Federal Government and, as such, neither makes evaluations nor draws conclusions as to the character or integrity of any organization, publication or individual.

key_findings.finding: A NICAP member reported suspecting the AFSCA newsletter of being communist-backed to J. Edgar Hoover, illustrating how Cold War anxieties became entangled with civilian UFO interest groups in FBI files.

quotes.text: Having received & read my first issue I feel it isn't just what it appears on the surface. I can't say just why, but with my limited idea of how communists operate it strikes me it is backed by them.
If, by writing for this AFSCA Report, my name could in anyway be aligned with the communist party, I would like to know if there is any wayI can get things straightened out.

key_findings.finding: The AFSCA's 3rd National Flying Saucer Convention (Reno, July 1966) assembled a broad roster of 'contactee' speakers claiming personal encounters with extraterrestrial beings, and the program was preserved in the FBI's case file.

key_findings.finding: The AFSCA newsletter published a 'channeled message' from an alleged extraterrestrial named 'Master Kalen-Li Retan' (of 'planet Korendor') that explicitly accused the U.S. government of being a 'military puppet' and the President of being 'a pawn'—the kind of content that would have drawn FBI monitoring attention during the Cold War.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: The 1977 White House memo explicitly references the Air Force closing its UFO investigation (Project Blue Book) and the resulting referral vacuum, directly informing the FBI's stated policy of routing sightings to the Air Force.

The White House inquiry from Jody Powell via the Office of Science and Technology Policy represents executive-branch-level scrutiny of interagency UFO coordination, touching the same oversight space as congressional inquiry.
